verdicts.note: Use another letter for the indeterminate on radix-digit-convolution (for example X), since z on exact-integer-multiplication is an integer below 2^k.
Use another letter for the shifted index (l-k) mod q on discrete-fourier-transform (for example r), since t on cyclic-convolution is the output index.
Use another letter for the binary string (for example w), since s on gaussian-resampling is the length of the source vectors.
Use another letter for the shifted index (for example r), since t on gaussian-resampling is the length of the target vectors.
Use another letter for the output index (for example o), since t on gaussian-resampling is the length of the target vectors.
Use another letter for the first integer (for example p), since u on gaussian-resampling is the length-s source vector used by the transform-identity page.
Use another letter for the target vector on gaussian-resampling, since b on radix-digit-convolution is the digit bit count.
Use another letter for the target vector on gaussian-resampling, since b on discrete-fourier-transform is the second convolution vector of length q, not a length-t target.
Use another letter for the target vector on gaussian-resampling, since b on cyclic-convolution is the second sequence of length q.
Use another letter for the padded output length (for example L), since k on gaussian-resampling is a target entry index.
Use another letter for the summation index over all integers on gaussian-resampling (for example m'), since i on radix-digit-convolution is a digit index running from 0 to m-1.
Use another letter for the last partial-sum index on gaussian-resampling (for example R), since M on operator-norm is a linear map.
Use another letter for the source map A=S (for example G), since A on transform-identity is the contraction S/2 = S' that operator-norm also uses.
Use another letter for the generic length-t vector on transform-identity (for example y), since v on radix-digit-convolution is the second integer.
